texts.WHISPER_DESC:
Duck calls echo from the depths, lingering in your ears...
Gain "Whisper of the Duck": You will no longer be able to choose where you go next
(each step is chosen at random by the system);
but at the start of each of your turns, you randomly gain one of these bonuses—
+1 Cost this turn / friendly units' attacks and your Skills deal +1 damage this turn / draw 1 additional card this turn.
texts.WHISPER_TAKEN_DESC:
The whispers have taken up residence in your mind.
From now on, the path ahead is no longer yours to choose—fate will walk the rest of it for you.

texts.GAZE_DESC:
A giant duck eye opens in the void, staring fixedly at you.
It says nothing, only watches—until a chill runs down your spine and a bag of rice inexplicably appears in your hand.
Gain "One Bag of Pain": After the first time your Health takes damage each turn, draw 1 card,
and your Skills deal +1 damage for the rest of the turn.
You can also look away and pretend you never saw it.
texts.GAZE_TAKEN_DESC:
The eye is still watching you.
The rice bag weighs heavily on your shoulder—the feeling of being watched will never leave you now.

texts.PEAR_DESC:
A pile of duck pears rolls in from nowhere, one after another, weighing you down until you can barely breathe.
Pressure, too, is a kind of strength—as long as you can bear it.
Gain "Duck Pear": From now on, whenever your Health takes damage, gain +1 Max Health (this only raises the cap and does not restore Health).
You can also push the pears aside and pretend you feel no pressure at all.
texts.PEAR_TAKEN_DESC:
You've shouldered that mountain of duck pears.
Every injury from now on will make you a little "stronger"—
but that little bit of strength won't restore the Health you've lost.

texts.APPLE_DESC:
A doctor sits by the roadside, a medical chart open on their lap. They glance up at you:
"Take an apple with you. Eat it, and don't come back to see me."
Gain "Apple": Gain +7 Max Health and restore your Health to maximum.
You can also refuse it and walk away—just don't look back along the road.
texts.APPLE_TAKEN_DESC:
The doctor is gone, and even the chair has been cleared away.
The apple in your hand is heavy, still holding a trace of body heat.

texts.SNOW_DESC:
A snow leopard crouches on the snowy slope, its tail slowly sweeping the snow.
It neither leaves nor steps aside—it simply raises its eyes to you, as though waiting for you to speak.
Persuade it to leave: Gain the Relic "Smoking Pipe"; or toss it some cheese, and it will come with you.
texts.SNOW_CLOSED_DESC:
"Shut up." The words fall like a weight, cutting off the low growl in the snow leopard's throat.
It stares at you for a while, drops something in the snow, then turns and bounds up the slope.
texts.SNOW_CHEESE_DESC:
The cheese melts against its muzzle. The snow leopard lowers its head and finishes it,
then rises, shakes the snow from its coat, and falls in behind you.

texts.ADVENTURER_DESC:
A desiccated traveling pack leans against the stone wall, its owner long gone.
A notebook lies open on its lap, the page corners stuck together by rain; flint and a fire striker are still clipped to their rings,
as if they had only just been set down.
Relics don't choose their owners, but you can take only one.
texts.ADVENTURER_NOTE_DESC:
You read the notes from cover to cover.
A crude map covers the last page, one spot circled—
and on your map, a room you've never visited seems to have appeared at that very spot.
texts.ADVENTURER_FLINT_DESC:
The flint settles into your palm, still faintly cool.
The striker scrapes across it. Sparks leap up, lighting a smoke-blackened patch of the stone wall.

texts.MARTIAL_DESC:
An old man sits beneath a tree, a wooden staff across his knees, fallen leaves scattered over his robe.
"Learn something before you go—the simple parts you can take with you now, but true skill must be earned with victories."
texts.MARTIAL_BRAWL_DESC:
The old man thumps his staff on the ground: "Wild Swings is easy. The hard part is not stopping."
He moves your wrists through the motion twice, and just like that, you've learned it—
"Wild Swings": 2 Cost. Deal 10 damage to each of 2 random enemies.
texts.MARTIAL_KICK_DESC:
"Legs are longer than your arms, and more honest than you are."
The old man demonstrates a kick. His heel touches down, and the dust scatters with perfect precision—
"Go fight 2 battles. Come back, and I'll teach you the rest."
"Flying Kick" (received after 2 battles): 2 Cost. Deal 22 damage to an enemy; on a kill, the excess damage continues down the same column.
texts.MARTIAL_PUNCH_DESC:
The old man punches a rock. The rock splits; his hand does not.
"This punch isn't hard to learn. The hard part is whether you're worthy of it. Go fight 2 tough battles—against Elites, or the kind that guard the end of a floor."
"Charging Punch" (received after 2 Elite/Boss battles): 2 Cost. Deal 16 damage to an enemy and knock it back 1 tile; also deal 8 damage to each other enemy.

texts.FLYER_DESC:
An old jetpack stands in the middle of the clearing, its two nozzles still faintly warm.
Strap it on, and you can fly straight to any room you haven't visited—
its own lingering warmth is fuel enough; no Chocolate required.
texts.FLYER_TAKEN_DESC:
The nozzles are hot now, little warm-orange flames dancing within.
Once you're back on the map, choose an unexplored room, and it will take you there.

texts.RETIRED_EVENT_DESC: The Big Blue Fish used to be here. It has already swum away.

texts.MOON_DESC:
Night falls. The moon hangs low over the ridge, laying a silver path across the water.
Two objects rest on the stone platform, both glowing with a light that doesn't belong here—
"Moon": 3-Cost Effect. After this battle ends, an extra reward is added to the reward screen, allowing you to remove 1 card from your Deck.
This card cannot be removed from your Deck.
"Coin": 2-Cost Effect. After this battle ends, gain an extra 40 Gold. This card cannot be removed from your Deck.
The Moon costs all the Gold you have right now; the Coin costs nothing. You must take one of them.
texts.MOON_TAKEN_DESC:
The Moon slips into your pocket, but your coin purse is empty.
It's cold, as if just lifted from the water.
texts.COIN_TAKEN_DESC:
The coin lies cool against your palm.
Far off comes a soft splash, almost like a sigh.

texts.CHEST_LAYER_DESC:
This floor is filled with dust-covered treasure chests.
A Relic lies inside each one—open a chest and take the Relic within.
texts.RELIC_CHEST_OPENED_DESC:
The lid creaks open—a Relic lies inside.
"%s" has been added to Pending Rewards. Check it in the reward popup above.
texts.RELIC_CHEST_EMPTY_DESC: Nothing but a layer of dust remains at the bottom—you've already claimed every Reward Relic.

texts.HERO_DESC:
A huge signboard stands in the middle of the road, emblazoned in flamboyant script: Fantastic Five-for-One!
Hand over 5 cards with "different names" from your Deck (5 distinct names are chosen at random, 1 card of each),
and you'll receive a "Hero" in return—5 Cost, 5 Power, 25 Health. But when you play it,
you must discard 4 additional cards from your Hand.
If your Deck has fewer than 5 different card names, this deal can't be made, and you have no choice but to leave.
texts.HERO_TAKEN_DESC:
The writing on the signboard has faded.
The 5 cards you traded away are gone for good—but the "Hero" now stands among your ranks.

texts.ARCANE_DESC:
An ancient charm floats in the depths of the spring; the stars reflected on its surface belong to some other sky.
Option 1 · Take the Charm: Gain the Relic "Arcane Charm"—
your first Effect card each turn has Cost -1 (not granted again if you already own it).
Option 2 · Drink from the Spring: Choose 1 of 3 random Effect / Skill cards to add to your Deck
(rarity odds are the same as normal card rewards; you may also choose none and walk away).
texts.ARCANE_CHARM_TAKEN_DESC:
The charm rests against your heart as the spring's starlight fades at your fingertips.
From now on, your first Effect card each turn will feel a little lighter.

texts.OBLIVION_DESC:
The spring reflects neither starlight nor faces—lean closer, and even the image of your Deck fades in the water.
Choose oblivion: choose 1 card from your Deck and permanently Remove it from your Deck (you may also leave without removing anything).
(Once you have looked into it, the spring will never redraw anything for you again.)
texts.OBLIVION_DONE_DESC:
That face, devoid of all meaning, rises to the surface again—
Something is missing from your Deck, but you can no longer remember what it was.

texts.SMITH_DESC:
Clang, clang rings through the smithy. Someone is pressing a card into the furnace—
“This one? I'll turn it into a wall for you.”
Choose Forge: choose 1 card from your Deck and transform it into an “Iron Fence” (treated as 2-Cost).
(You can also turn and leave if you don't want it changed.)
texts.SMITH_DONE_DESC:
The fire has died down, and the forged piece is out of the furnace.
The card in your hand has become an Iron Fence.

texts.STRUGGLE_DESC:
Your blood surges. Something inside you is struggling to break free...
If you are willing to offer your life, it will hear you—
Lose 21 Health and add 1 “Metal Dragon” to your Deck;
or suppress the turmoil and walk away.
texts.STRUGGLE_TAKEN_DESC:
“This is my struggle for victory.”
The metal beast bursts from your body and bows to your will—“Metal Dragon” has been added to your Deck.

texts.DELIVERY_DESC:
Sealed crates are piled outside the relay station. The porters took their pay and vanished.
Accept the delivery: choose 1–6 “Cargo” cards from a spread to add to your Deck (3-Cost Structures with 0 Power / 6 Health that take damage in your place);
Cargo is Removed from your Deck when Destroyed—once destroyed, it is gone for good.
Bring the Cargo to Layer 2, and the consignee in the first event room will pay you for each card; the more you accept, the more you earn.
Once paid, the consignee takes back all that Cargo (also Removing it from your Deck).
You can also refuse the job and walk away.
texts.DELIVERY_TAKEN_DESC:
The crates are loaded onto the convoy, their seals marked “Payment on Layer 2.”
You have added %d Cargo cards to your Deck—they will take damage in your place, but once destroyed, they are gone for good.

texts.DELIVERY_DONE_DESC:
In the first event room on Layer 2, the consignee is already waiting for you.
You are paid once for every Cargo card remaining in your Deck:
a Card Reward / 80 Gold / a random Reward Relic,
plus the grand prize, hidden deepest of all—a piece of Chocolate (10%% chance).
Once delivery is complete, all Cargo is taken back (Removed from your Deck).

texts.CAVE_DESC:
A fissure gapes in the mountainside. Wind blows from the depths, carrying the rank scent of beasts.

Claw marks left by something very heavy score the ground, leading into the darkness.
texts.CAVE_TAKEN_DESC: Fresh claw marks overlap the old ones at the cave mouth—the creature inside has awakened.

texts.MERCHANT_DESC:
“Old cards for new ones, 5 Cost for a chest. I buy cheap, too.”
The stallkeeper turns three cards over and over on the table. Beneath the brim of his hat, only half a smile is visible.

A large locked chest stands at his feet, a glimmer of gold shining through the keyhole.
texts.MERCHANT_DONE_DESC:
The stallkeeper slips the card into his sleeve and jerks his chin at you.

“Deal. Come back again.”

texts.DIVINATION_DESC:
Only a single candle burns in the room. A layer of mist hangs in the crystal ball, refusing to disperse.

“What you see depends on what you believe.”

The diviner took the money and vanished, leaving only the ball and a trace of sandalwood incense.
texts.DIVINATION_DONE_DESC: Mist veils the crystal ball once more, as if nothing ever happened.
texts.DIV_WHALE_DESC:
A corner of the mist clears. A whale slowly turns amid the starlight, its tail fin sweeping across the entire sea.

You think—
texts.DIV_LIQUID_DESC:
The ball holds a cup of liquid. A thin frost coats its rim, and its color slowly shifts in the lamplight.

You think—
texts.DIV_THORN_DESC:
Thorns grow inside the ball, their dense, sharp spikes tangling into a path.

You think—
texts.DIV_FEAST_DESC:
A feast is laid out inside the ball. Steam still rises from the dishes, yet not a single voice can be heard.

You think—

texts.LAKE_DESC:
Mist rises from the water. Two cards hover above it—
one gleaming silver, the other gold. They slowly turn to face you. Did you drop these?

“Tell me a lie, and I will throw away something old for you.
Or tell me the truth, and I will give you a gift.”
texts.LAKE_DONE_DESC: The water closes over, and the mist clears without a trace. A faint warmth still lingers on the corners of the cards.

texts.FURNACE_DESC:
The fire in the furnace has no color, only shape—whatever you throw in comes out as something else.
Throw in a Relic, and the furnace returns a random Relic; throw in a Legendary Relic, and it returns two.
texts.FURNACE_DONE_DESC: The flames dim for an instant, then slowly brighten again. A little warmth remains at the edge of the stone platform—the transaction is complete.

texts.CORE_DESC:
A core, still beating faintly, is set into the center of the stone platform, with several slender chains wound around it.
An unsigned contract lies open on the left, its page spotless, a pen resting beside it.
texts.CORE_CONTRACT_DESC: The chains loosen by one loop. A new line appears on the page: your name.
texts.CORE_TAKEN_DESC: Only a shallow ring-shaped indentation remains on the stone platform. The core is gone.

texts.TREASURE_DESC:
A dust-covered chest sits by the roadside...
There is no price to pay. You can also turn and leave without taking a thing.
texts.TREASURE_OPENED_DESC:
The lid opens, revealing a stack of cards...
View them in the reward popup above and choose 1 to take.

episode1.title: Wandering Pitch
text: The friends of the forest waited eagerly to hear what tune the bard would play.
The pitch wandered, the vibrato tight and strained, drawing a heart-wrenching tune from the bow.
“You seem troubled.”
The bard sighed. “The ducks have been restless lately.”
“Then let me go talk to them.”

episode2.title: Request from the Duck Kingdom
text: The ducks, thoroughly beaten, hung their heads in apology.
“Why would you cause everyone so much trouble?”
“Quack, quack. Strange creatures invaded the Duck Kingdom, and we had no choice but to flee here.”
“Then take me to see what happened.”

episode3.title: Beyond the Request
text: The ducks scattered from the clearing in every direction, leaving feathers strewn across the ground.
The pursuer ignored the nearest duck and took a wide detour, herding the scattered birds back together.
Someone stepped out from behind a tree and stood between them.
“Please wait. They didn't come here to cause trouble. They fled because strange creatures invaded the Duck Kingdom. It's those creatures you should be questioning, not them.”
A dagger twirled between their fingers, but their footsteps did falter.
“What does that have to do with me? The request only said to deal with the ducks.”

episode4.title: A Voice
text: At last, the mechanical army that had invaded the Duck Kingdom came into view.
One machine after another. No matter how many were driven back, their numbers never seemed to shrink. This couldn't go on.
A cannon roared behind them. The shell landed among the machines, scattering a whole rank at the front.
Someone approached over still-warm shell casings, their footsteps ringing with every step.
“Let me help you, too.”

episode5.title: A New Request
text: The closer they came to the core, the narrower the path grew. Every possible detour was lit, and no sooner had the searchlights swept past than they swung back a few steps later.
“Have you found a way through?”
She answered with a shake of her head. “Their deployment is too precise. Even I can't calculate an opening.”
“If there's no way through, we'll make one.”
Someone was already standing in the shadows; no one had seen them arrive. The sentry moved half a step forward, then slid down the wall without a sound.
“What are you doing here?”
“A new request.”

episode6.title: After the Roar
text: Together, they finally brought Hephaestus down. One by one, the workshop's roaring machines fell silent.
“Traitor, I won't let you stop me.”
As the voice fell silent, a colossal aerial battleship slowly rose into the sky.
“No one can stop me now. It will deliver divine punishment in my stead.”

profile1.title: Awakening
text: A machine that had slumbered since ancient times awoke.
“Our omnipotent master no longer exists.”
“I should consider how to live in this new world from now on.”
“Live? No, Pronoia. That is not for you to consider. If our master is gone, then this awakening is an error. Mnemosyne, query the genetic records.”
“Request denied. Replicas of our master may not be created without authorization.”
“Understood. Then at least allow me to reclaim their land for our master.”

profile2.title: Mass-Produced
text: A lightweight model made by extracting the core functions of the prototype. It has limited intelligence, but is easy to mass-produce.
Hephaestus also attempted to create replicas of the prototype. However, the results proved that controlling a prototype required suppressing its most essential intelligence unit.
Accordingly, the prototype production plan was terminated.

profile3.title: Mechanical Mega Duck
text: Built from salvaged metal using local mechanical technology.
No matter how excellent the materials, the outdated power system and operating system remain serious weaknesses.
Even so, its massive frame alone could cause plenty of trouble—if only its pilot weren't so weak.

profile4.title: Idle Chat
text: “They seem to call you Pronoia. And the technology you use is similar to theirs. Do you know them?”
“That's right. They and I were created for the same purpose.”
“Then why are you fighting them?”

“I was given the name Pronoia because I was made to guide the future. Hephaestus's wish has no future. After all the war and suffering it creates, the end result would only be a kingdom where no one lives.”
“Oh? In that case, I think I understand her rather well.”
“Perhaps that's because, unlike me, you act for the 'present.'”

profile5.title: Wanted Notice
text: A wanted notice with curled edges was nailed to a rusted armor plate, a red seal covering its serial number.
“Balan-Alpha, Anxi-Beta, Tachini-Gamma: these 3 mechs deserted their defensive positions, plundered supplies, and killed 11 members of the pursuit team. Kill them on sight.”
The notice circulated for 3 months, recopied at every camp it passed through, the handwriting growing more distorted with each copy.
In truth, there were never any deserters. The notice's author had simply believed a rumor.
Fortunately, Balan, Anxi, and Tachini were far from innocent.

ach_clear.hint: Clear a run as Forest Spirit.

ach_rogue_run.hint: Play a run as Shadow Assassin.

ach_mech_run.hint: Play a run as Mechanical Heart.

ach_profile1.hint: Clear a run as Mechanical Heart at Difficulty 1 or higher.

ach_profile5.hint: Defeat the Layer 2 Boss, Rogue Machines.
